Simple tips to help you cut utility costs.
HVAC: point your vents toward the outside wall or windows as this is where the heat comes in. It will lower your bill and your unit will not have to work as hard extending its life.

Floor length heavy curtains can be used in winter time across windows and doorways to control the flow of heat in a home. Especially if you live in an older home, your house probably has lots of doors that you have taken down, not understanding that they are meant for temperature control.

Also don't forget to dress for the weather. Adding or removing layers should be the goto most of the year.
Heavy curtains also block heat from entering in the summer, not just cold in the winter. The white plastic light-blocking curtains will also help reflect heat out of the house.
LED bulbs are great for fixtures you leave on every night or 24 hours. Otherwise, the amortized cost is typically higher than a CF.

If your central air vents don't have damperers, then you want some of these or these (cheaper). Now you no longer have to pay to central heat/cool rooms that you aren't using. Get in the habit of closing the dampers in the kids' room when they get up, in your bedroom when you get up, etc.

Thermostat placement can make a big difference too. When I bought my current house, the thermostat was right in-line with, and between, the front door and back door (which happen to be in the same living area). So whenever the front or back door opened the thermostat would get blasted with air from outside, and would thus trigger the central heat/cooling. I moved the fucker over a room and it made a significant difference in my utility costs. It's easy to move a thermostat - it's just a few small low-voltage wires. If you aren't comfortable moving it yourself then it'd be cheap to hire someone to do it (and would pay for itself within a few months at worst).

Speaking of thermostats, get a programmable one. Not a fucking $300 Apple iBlow or whatever the new trendy looking ones are that record you masturbating, just a cheap 7-day programmable one. This one's $20. It takes an hour tops to replace your old one and program the new one. You can't hurt yourself doing it - it doesn't have any high voltage or dangerous wires. Just read the instructions and verify that you are connecting the color-coded wires as directed. If you don't already know, these things let you set temperatures for different times of each day of the week. So you can have all heating/cooling cut off at 4:00 AM (hot? cold? get out of bed you lazy bastard), then you can have it turn back on 30 minutes before you get home from work. If the wife is at home all day, adjust accordingly. Utilizing a programmable thermometer can save you a LOT of money.

You can also set your thermostat temperature higher (if it's hot out) and buy a few box fans. Box fans use very little electricity in comparison and effectively cool you off for much less money. The down side is that they're noisy when turned up high, and they look pretty niggery. Here's one for $17.

If it's cold out, same thing, but lower the temperature on your thermostat and use a cheap space heater. This will save money if you only need to heat one or two rooms - diminishing returns start to set in after that. Here's a cheap one for $19. Electric blankets are a thing too and are typically more efficient than space heaters.

Your water heater has a heat setting on it. There is a sticker on the front of your unit that explains more. If you have it set higher than it needs to be then you are wasting money. Try turning it down a little and then wait a day or two. If everyone still has enough hot water when they shower, and the faucet in the kitchen is still hot enough, then turn it down a little more and repeat. Staggering your household's showering times (morning vs. night, etc.) will allow you to turn it down further. Also, buy some inexpensive water-efficient showerheads.

Use rags instead of paper towels; wash them in a full load with bleach (as directed). Cloth diapers work just fine and are reusable and your baby will probably like them better too - wash em with the cleanup rags.

Fuck the dishwasher. It's honestly a waste of time and money. Rubbermaid makes drying racks that don't look like shit for $5. Never pay for dishwasher detergent again.
